questions.question: How does an exhaust heat exchanger function to heat the cabin of an aircraft and what are the major concerns with the system during inspection?
questions.idealAnswer: It is used mostly on small engine light aircraft. The exhaust is routed through a shroud and the exhaust gases are separate from either ram air (in flight) or fan on the Ground) the heat from the exhaust heats up the ambient air or (heat exchanges) and is directed into the cabin. The major concern while inspecting is that cracks can form in the exhaust, and leak exhaust gasses and mix with the ambient air and be directed into the cabin. Even a small crack could cause enough exhaust gasses (carbon dioxide/carbon monoxide) into the cabin to be fatal. Typically during inspection, the exhaust system is pressurized and checked for leaks to ensure their are no cracks.

questions.question: What is a combustion heater and describe any criterion for inspection of a combustion heater that may be particularly important?
questions.idealAnswer: A combustion heater is an independent heat source from the aircraft engines. It is used on small to medium size aircraft. The combustion heater has a combustion chamber and a shroud, ambient air (ram air) or fan air on the ground, is ducted between the shroud and the combustion chamber Absorbing heat and directed into the cabin. Exhaust is directed overboard. During inspection it is important to check for fuel leaks and any cracks in the combustion chamber that could lead to fuel vapors or carbon monoxide entering the cabin.

questions.question: Briefly describe the vapor cycle of a vapor cycle air conditioning system.
questions.idealAnswer: A vapor cycle air conditioning system is a closed system with refrigerant in it. It is used to transfer heat from inside the cabin to outside the cabin. Heat energy is moved from the cabin air into liquid refrigerant by blowing cabin air over a heat exchanger (evaporator) containing refrigerant. The vapor is then compressed, due to the additional energy, the vapor becomes very hot. The very hot vapor is then routed to different heat exchanger (condenser,) where the vapor turns to a liquid or (condenses.)Then the heat from the refrigerant is transferred to the outside. The cycle is than repeated (Vapor Cycle.) Components of the vapor cycle system are as follows: Evaporator, Compressor, condenser, receiver dryer, expansion valve. Be prepared to discuss the function of each component with the examiner.

questions.question: Briefly describe how an air cycle air conditioning system provides cool air to the aircraft cabin.
questions.idealAnswer: Turbine engine bleed air is conditioned for use in the cabin during air cycle air conditioning. Turbine engine bleed air is let into the system where it then is routed to an air to air heat exchanger that cools bleed air with ambient ram air. The cooled bleed air is then directed into a compressor of the air cycle machine (ACM.) There it is compressed before flowing through a secondary air to air heat exchanger that again cools the air with ambient ram air. The bleed air flows back into the (ACM) where it drives an expansion turbine. This cools the air even further. Water is then removed via a water separator and the bleed air is then mixed with bypassed hot bleed air, and sent to the cabin at a temperature requested by the crew. Be prepared to discuss each component with the examiner. Each component of the air cycle machine(ACM) are as follows: Primary heat exchanger, secondary heat exchanger, compressor, expansion turbine, 35degree bypass valve, and a water separator.

questions.question: Explain the two basic modes of cabin pressurization and name the single component that modulates to control the pressure of the air in the cabin during both modes of operation.
questions.idealAnswer: Two modes are isobaric mode and differential pressure mode. In isobaric mode, the pressurization system works to maintain a single pressure inside the cabin, known as cabin altitude, despite the altitude of the aircraft or the pressure of the ambient air outside the aircraft. In differential mode, the system controls the cabin pressure to maintain a constant pressure difference between the air inside the cabin and the air outside the aircraft regardless of altitude changes. The single device that opens and closes, or modulates to control air exiting the cabin, and thus, the air pressure in the cabin is the outflow valve.

questions.question: What type of oxygen system is typically used on light, general aviation aircraft and what type(s) is used on transport category aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: Many light aircraft do not have an oxygen system if the aircraft is not designed to fly at altitudes that require oxygen. Some small general aviation aircraft may have a portable oxygen bottle on board to be used by the crew when desired. A built in system may exist that uses approved containers of gaseous oxygen. Both are typically delivered through regulated, continuous flow systems where oxygen is supplied at a steady rate when the valve of the oxygen container is opened. However, electronic pulse demand oxygen delivery systems are currently available for general aviation aircraft. These type pulse oxygen system only delivers oxygen to the user when they inhale creating a demand- type system. Oxygen is carried on transport category aircraft for emergency purposes only. During normal operation the cabin pressure provides enough oxygen for the crew and passengers. Gaseous and solid oxygen are used in an emergencies when pressurization is lost. The gaseous oxygen is stored in remote, pressurized tanks and routed to the users thorough a system of tubes. Solid oxygen generators produce gaseous oxygen for use when ignited. Passengers receive the oxygen from either source through a continuous flow delivery system. Most crew oxygen is delivered via demand flow or pressure- demand flow type regulators.

questions.question: Name some precautions when performing maintenance on aircraft oxygen systems.
questions.idealAnswer: Always keep clothing, hands, and tools clean, make sure there is no grease or oily residue around or near oxygen when servicing. A good maintenance practice is to have dedicated tools for servicing oxygen only. Never smoke or have an open flame within 50 feet of the work area when servicing oxygen. Always use protective plugs or caps when working with oxygen cylinders, system components or plumbing. Do not use any kind of adhesive tape. Oxygen cylinders should be stored in a designated, cool, ventilated area in the hanger away from petroleum products or heat sources. Fittings should be turned slowly to allow any residual pressure to dissipate. All oxygen lines should be marked and should have at least two inches of clearance from moving parts, electrical wiring, and all fluid lines. A pressure leak check must be performed each time the system is opened for maintenance. Do not use any lubricants, sealers, cleaners, etc., unless specifically approved for oxygen use.
